non_authority: This proposal is an independent literary segmentation input only. It does not decide canonical, theological, historical, source-critical, harmonizing, or project-authority questions.
routing_principle: Prefer observable scene, speaker, audience, setting, discourse-form, quotation, temporal, and closure transitions; preserve coherent embedded forms when a larger rhetorical sequence governs them.

macro_parents.label: Jerusalem entry, controversies, and public discourse
Arrest, trial, death, burial, and final scenes

hot_zones.issue: Genealogy, dream reports, journeys, and citation-shaped closures create nested seams.
Long red-letter discourse contains repeated formulaic subforms and a narrator closure.
Rapid scene alternation makes participant and setting resets decisive.
Final sayings continue directly into the narrator discourse closure.
Questions, denunciation, prayer-like address, disputes, and family scene are densely adjacent.
Public parables, private explanations, and hometown narrative alternate.
Retrospective death report turns abruptly into withdrawal and provision.
Recognition dialogue, forecast, mountain vision, and explanatory dialogue interlock.
A question, illustrative narrative, application, and formal discourse closure form one arc.
Encounter, private commentary, and vineyard illustration share one governing exchange.
Challenge dialogue and successive illustrative narratives are linked within one controversy cycle.
Audience address, repeated woes, and city lament invite competing boundaries.
Prompted discourse contains forecast, warnings, analogies, illustrative narratives, judgment tableau, and narrator closure.
Three linked readiness illustrations can be split by form or retained by shared exhortive function.
Judgment tableau ends immediately in the formal closure and transition.
Meal, forecasts, prayer, arrest, hearing, denial, and remorse are tightly sequenced.
Death, observers, burial, guard report, discovery, counter-report, and final meeting rapidly alternate.
Red letters, headings, and paragraph breaks are used only as supporting evidence, never controlling authority.

units.title: Genealogy from Abraham to Jesus
units.deciding_marker: The opening label initiates a patterned descent list, and verse 17 totals its three movements.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the following birth account would blur the list-to-narrative form change.
units.defensible_basis: The formulaic ancestry chain and closing enumeration make an independently defensible literary unit.

units.title: Joseph's dream and the naming of Jesus
units.deciding_marker: A new origin formula shifts to Joseph's predicament; waking, obedience, and naming close the scene.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting the embedded quotation from the dream would interrupt the messenger's explanation.
units.defensible_basis: Scene, speech, quotation, and narrated compliance form one compact dream report.

units.title: Visitors from the east
units.deciding_marker: A Bethlehem time-setting introduces new travelers; their redirected journey ends with worship and departure by another route.
units.rejected_alternative: Extending through verse 15 would merge their completed visit with a new dream and different journey.
units.defensible_basis: Stable participants and a resolved travel quest support the span.

units.title: Flight to Egypt
units.deciding_marker: After their departure, another dream changes the actor and destination; arrival and residence complete the command.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the massacre would conflate Joseph's escape scene with Herod's reaction scene.
units.defensible_basis: Temporal reset, dream instruction, and exact compliance form a short episode.

units.title: Herod's massacre
units.literary_form: royal reaction narrative with lament quotation
units.deciding_marker: Herod's realization initiates violent action, followed by a lament-shaped interpretive close.
units.rejected_alternative: Absorbing the next dream would obscure the switch from Herod's act to Joseph's return.
units.defensible_basis: Actor focus and concluding lament distinguish the episode.

units.title: Return and settlement in Nazareth
units.deciding_marker: Herod's death triggers a return command; a second warning redirects the family, ending in settled residence.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting at verse 21 would detach the redirection that determines the episode's endpoint.
units.defensible_basis: The paired travel decisions resolve the infancy movement geographically.

units.title: John's proclamation and baptism activity
units.deciding_marker: A new temporal and geographic opening introduces John; public address and announced successor remain under his activity.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at verse 6 would detach the direct speech that develops the same public scene.
units.defensible_basis: Shared speaker, setting, audience, and proclamation form govern the span.

units.title: Jesus baptized
units.deciding_marker: Jesus arrives as a new focal participant; dialogue, baptism, opened heavens, and heavenly voice culminate together.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining chapter 4 would merge the river epiphany with a wilderness testing sequence.
units.defensible_basis: Arrival-to-voice progression supplies a strong scene arc.

units.title: Testing in the wilderness
units.deciding_marker: The Spirit-led setting initiates a repeated challenge-response pattern; the tempter's departure and angelic arrival close it.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting each test separately would understate the deliberate threefold escalation.
units.defensible_basis: Repeated speech form, stable opponents, and explicit exit unify the passage.

units.title: Withdrawal to Galilee and opening proclamation
units.deciding_marker: News of John's arrest prompts relocation, followed by a residence notice and a summarized public message.
units.rejected_alternative: Extending into the call scenes would mix summary proclamation with individual encounters.
units.defensible_basis: Relocation and the inaugural speech formula cohere before participant-specific scenes.

units.title: Calling two pairs of brothers
units.deciding_marker: Walking beside the sea initiates two parallel call-and-immediate-response episodes.
units.rejected_alternative: Separating the pairs is possible, but their repeated syntax creates a compact diptych.
units.defensible_basis: Parallel summons and immediate departure strongly bind the two calls.

units.title: Galilean activity and crowds
units.deciding_marker: Generalized teaching, proclamation, healing, fame, and crowd movement replace the prior individual scenes.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining chapter 5 would merge an itinerary summary with a newly staged discourse.
units.defensible_basis: Durative verbs and geographic catalog mark a summary unit.

units.title: Opening blessings
units.deciding_marker: Mountain seating and disciple approach open the speech; repeated blessing clauses form a self-contained sequence.
units.rejected_alternative: Including verses 13-16 would merge blessing pronouncements with direct public-function metaphors.
units.defensible_basis: Repeated form and a concluding expanded address delimit the opening movement.

units.title: Salt and light sayings
units.deciding_marker: Second-person metaphors shift the discourse from blessings to public-function images, ending in a purpose clause.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining verse 17 would cross into an explicit topic-reset formula.
units.defensible_basis: Shared imagery and direct address yield a brief coherent exhortation.

units.title: Law-and-righteousness program
units.deciding_marker: A prohibition against a mistaken inference opens a concentrated declaration and closes with an entry condition.
units.rejected_alternative: Merging with the first contrast would weaken the program-to-example transition.
units.defensible_basis: Opening correction and closing criterion frame this paragraph.

units.title: Anger, reconciliation, and settlement
units.deciding_marker: The first heard-saying formula initiates a legal contrast expanded by two reconciliation illustrations.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting at verse 22 would detach applications that define the teaching's practical shape.
units.defensible_basis: Formulaic opening and coherent conflict vocabulary support the unit.

units.title: Adultery and drastic avoidance
units.deciding_marker: A renewed heard-saying formula changes the topic; paired eye-and-hand hyperboles close the warning.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the divorce saying would merge related but formally reintroduced material.
units.defensible_basis: Topic reset plus balanced paired warnings create a clear subunit.

units.title: Divorce saying
units.deciding_marker: A fresh saying-introduction creates a compact rule and counterstatement.
units.rejected_alternative: Absorbing it into the prior unit would ignore its independent citation formula.
units.defensible_basis: Its explicit introduction and compressed scope justify a distinct unit.

units.title: Oaths and truthful speech
units.deciding_marker: Another heard-saying formula opens; a catalog of prohibited oath objects resolves in a yes-or-no maxim.
units.rejected_alternative: Extending into retaliation would cross a repeated discourse reset.
units.defensible_basis: Formula, catalog, and aphoristic close delimit the passage.

units.title: Retaliation sayings
units.deciding_marker: A new heard-saying formula introduces non-retaliatory responses in a four-example series.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the enemy-love unit would flatten a separate formula and address pattern.
units.defensible_basis: The repeated situational imperatives create one example chain.

units.title: Enemy-love teaching
units.deciding_marker: The final heard-saying formula turns to enemies, prayer, divine impartiality, and a climactic completeness saying.
units.rejected_alternative: Combining all six contrasts would be defensible macroscopically but less precise at the repeated reset.
units.defensible_basis: A final formula, sustained rationale, and climactic imperative form a unit.

units.title: Almsgiving, prayer, and fasting
units.deciding_marker: A general warning introduces three matched when-you-do patterns, each contrasting display with hidden practice; fasting completes the triad.
units.rejected_alternative: Separating the model prayer from its surrounding pattern would lose its placement inside the prayer member.
units.defensible_basis: Repeated vocabulary, parallel reward closures, and three practices govern the unit.

units.title: Treasure, sight, and masters
units.deciding_marker: A shift to possession imagery begins with treasure, continues through the eye saying, and ends with the two-masters antithesis.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the anxiety section would merge compact maxims with an extended exhortation triggered by therefore.
units.defensible_basis: Shared concern with allegiance and possession links three aphoristic forms.

units.title: Do not be anxious
units.deciding_marker: Therefore opens a sustained prohibition developed through birds, lilies, and repeated questions; the final day saying closes it.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting birds and lilies would obscure their parallel argumentative role.
units.defensible_basis: Repeated anxiety vocabulary and two natural examples form a continuous appeal.

units.title: Judgment, self-examination, and discernment
units.deciding_marker: A prohibition on judging opens a measure saying and eye metaphor, followed by a compact discernment warning.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at verse 5 would isolate verse 6, but both concern discriminating perception after the same reset.
units.defensible_basis: Imperatives and linked discernment imagery give the paragraph defensible cohesion.

units.title: Ask, seek, knock
units.deciding_marker: Three imperatives introduce promised responses, a parent-child analogy, and a concluding therefore maxim.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining verse 13 would cross from assurance and reciprocity to a new gate metaphor.
units.defensible_basis: Repetition, analogy, and summary maxim form a rounded movement.

units.title: Two ways and true recognition
units.deciding_marker: The narrow-gate imperative begins paired alternatives, followed by tree-fruit tests and a profession-versus-performance warning.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting at verse 20 is plausible, but the recognition motif carries into the final warning.
units.defensible_basis: Binary contrasts and recognition criteria link the warnings.

units.title: Two builders and discourse closure
units.deciding_marker: Therefore introduces paired builders as the speech's final contrast; the narrator then records completion and crowd response.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at verse 27 would detach the formal closure that marks the unit's book-level seam.
units.defensible_basis: Concluding analogy plus explicit discourse-end formula establish the boundary.

units.title: Cleansing a leper
units.deciding_marker: Descent from the mountain and an approaching petitioner open a new scene; touch, cleansing, and instruction complete it.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the next healing would blur a participant and location reset.
units.defensible_basis: Approach-request-response-command provides a complete encounter.

units.title: Centurion's servant
units.deciding_marker: Entry into Capernaum brings a new petitioner; extended authority dialogue culminates in remote healing at that hour.
units.rejected_alternative: Separating the wider saying from the encounter would interrupt Jesus' response to the centurion.
units.defensible_basis: New setting, sustained dialogue, and narrated outcome bind the episode.

units.title: Healings at Peter's house
units.deciding_marker: Entry into Peter's house begins an individual healing that broadens into an evening summary and quotation-shaped close.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at verse 15 would detach the generalized expansion situated at the same house.
units.defensible_basis: Place continuity and individual-to-summary progression support the span.

units.title: Would-be followers
units.deciding_marker: Seeing crowds prompts departure; two would-be followers receive parallel, demanding replies before embarkation.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the lake event would combine shore dialogue with an enacted voyage scene.
units.defensible_basis: Two approach-and-response exchanges share the departure frame.

units.title: Storm calmed
units.deciding_marker: Boat entry opens the voyage; danger, plea, rebuke, calm, and marveling create a complete dramatic arc.
units.rejected_alternative: Extending into verse 28 would cross a landing and participant reset.
units.defensible_basis: Stable setting and problem-resolution structure mark the episode.

units.title: Two demoniacs and the swine
units.deciding_marker: Arrival on the far shore introduces two threatening figures; dialogue and expulsion end with a townwide request for departure.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting the townspeople's response would omit the public consequence of the same event.
units.defensible_basis: Geographic arrival, confrontation, transfer, and communal response form one scene.

units.title: Paralytic forgiven and healed
units.deciding_marker: Crossing back and entering the city resets the setting; a healing pronouncement provokes inner objection, ending in cure and crowd response.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the next call scene would merge a controversy-healing with a roadside summons.
units.defensible_basis: Problem, controversy, demonstrative act, and response close cleanly.

units.title: Matthew called and table controversy
units.deciding_marker: Moving on introduces a named toll collector; immediate following develops into a meal question answered with proverb and citation.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at verse 9 would detach the controversy generated by the new association.
units.defensible_basis: Call, table setting, objection, and reply form an integrated scene.

units.title: Question about fasting
units.deciding_marker: A new group approaches with a fasting question; bridegroom, cloth, and wineskin images answer it.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the following ruler scene would cross an explicit participant and request reset.
units.defensible_basis: Question plus three coordinated images create a discrete exchange.

units.title: Ruler's daughter and hemorrhaging woman
units.deciding_marker: A ruler's plea initiates a journey interrupted by another healing; the original destination resumes and closes with the girl's rising and spreading report.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting the interruption would obscure the deliberate nested narrative construction.
units.defensible_basis: Enclosure of the inner healing by the outer request and resolution unifies the span.

units.title: Two blind men
units.deciding_marker: Departure brings following petitioners whose request continues indoors; touch, restored sight, warning, and report complete the scene.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the mute-man episode would merge distinct petitioners and responses.
units.defensible_basis: Participant continuity and cure-to-publicity arc delimit it.

units.title: Mute demoniac and divided reactions
units.deciding_marker: As the healed men leave, a new afflicted person is brought; restored speech produces contrasting crowd and opponent responses.
units.rejected_alternative: Absorbing it into the prior healing would overlook the explicit departure-arrival pivot.
units.defensible_basis: New entrant, new impairment, and paired reactions create a compact unit.

units.title: Compassion for the crowds
units.deciding_marker: A generalized itinerary resumes; seeing the crowds prompts compassion imagery and a direct saying to disciples.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining chapter 10 would blur summary-and-prompt with the formal naming and commissioning scene.
units.defensible_basis: Durative summary broadens into a harvest saying that prepares, but does not enact, the commission.

units.title: Authority and names of the twelve
units.deciding_marker: Summoning the twelve opens the commission, grants authority, and supplies the complete named list.
units.rejected_alternative: Including verse 5 would merge roster form with direct mission instructions.
units.defensible_basis: Call, authorization, and list form make a clear introductory unit.

units.title: Mission destination and reception instructions
units.deciding_marker: The named group is sent with direct route, message, provision, lodging, and reception commands, ending in a rejection consequence.
units.rejected_alternative: Extending through verse 23 would join immediate travel procedure to a forecast of hostile hearings.
units.defensible_basis: Imperative sequence and reception motif supply internal cohesion.

units.title: Sent among wolves
units.deciding_marker: Behold marks a sheep-among-wolves image and shifts to future handing-over, testimony, family division, endurance, and flight.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the preceding logistics would mute the future-oriented warning reset.
units.defensible_basis: Forecast grammar and repeated hostile settings distinguish this unit.

units.title: Disciple and teacher; fear and acknowledgment
units.deciding_marker: A student-teacher maxim begins a new reasoning block, developed by repeated do-not-fear commands and acknowledgment contrasts.
units.rejected_alternative: Extending to verse 39 would cross the explicit do-not-think reset and household-conflict imagery.
units.defensible_basis: Proverb, repeated reassurance, and paired public-response sayings cohere.

units.title: Division, allegiance, reception, and discourse closure
units.literary_form: closing demand-and-reward sequence with narrator coda
units.deciding_marker: Do not think opens sharp relational contrasts; allegiance and reception sayings lead directly to the formal completion formula and departure.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at 10:42 would detach the narrator's explicit closure of the commissioned speech.
units.defensible_basis: Escalating parallel sayings and the discourse coda define a major seam.

units.title: John's question and Jesus' answer
units.deciding_marker: News received in confinement prompts John to send a two-part question; Jesus answers with a report list and concluding blessing.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the crowd address would merge a private messenger exchange with speech after their departure.
units.defensible_basis: Messenger arrival, reply, and implied return form a closed exchange.

units.title: Jesus addresses the crowds about John
units.deciding_marker: As the messengers leave, audience and topic shift to repeated what-did-you-go-out questions, evaluation, and a generation comparison.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting at verse 15 would detach the generation parable that completes the public assessment.
units.defensible_basis: Departure cue, repeated questions, and comparative close unite the address.

units.title: Woes to unresponsive towns
units.deciding_marker: Then marks a turn toward named towns; repeated woe and comparative judgment clauses form a compact series.
units.rejected_alternative: Merging with verses 25-30 would combine denunciation with a new direct address and invitation.
units.defensible_basis: Named-town parallels and repeated comparison language establish the unit.

units.title: Thanksgiving and invitation
units.deciding_marker: At that time introduces an address to the Father, a relational declaration, and a come-to-me appeal ending in rest.
units.rejected_alternative: Separating verse 28 would sever the invitation from its preceding self-disclosure.
units.defensible_basis: First-person address and invitation share a concentrated, climactic voice.

units.title: Grain plucking on the Sabbath
units.deciding_marker: A Sabbath field setting opens with an accusation; two precedents and a concluding lordship saying answer it.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the synagogue dispute would merge two related controversies across a new location.
units.defensible_basis: Field setting, objection, cited examples, and verdict form one scene.

units.title: Man with a withered hand
units.deciding_marker: Departure into their synagogue resets the scene; a test question, analogy, command, healing, and conspiracy complete it.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at verse 13 would omit the opponents' reaction that closes the controversy.
units.defensible_basis: Location change and action-reaction arc delimit the unit.

units.title: Withdrawal, healings, and quietness
units.deciding_marker: Awareness of the plot prompts departure and broad healing; a command for silence flows into a sustained quotation-shaped close.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the next exorcism would cross from summary and citation into a new brought-person scene.
units.defensible_basis: Causal withdrawal, generalized action, and quotation form a transition unit.

units.title: Exorcism dispute and words
units.deciding_marker: A possessed man is brought and healed; crowd reaction triggers an accusation answered by kingdom, strong-man, tree-fruit, and speech-account sayings.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at verse 30 would detach the ensuing speech tests from the same accusation-response argument.
units.defensible_basis: Event, accusation, extended rebuttal, and concluding words verdict form one controversy block.

units.title: Demand for a sign
units.deciding_marker: Some scribes and Pharisees initiate a new request; Jesus responds with sign, comparative, and returning-spirit illustrations.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting after verse 42 would isolate an analogy that completes the warning to this generation.
units.defensible_basis: New interlocutor formula and generation refrain govern the response.

units.title: Jesus' family seeks him
units.deciding_marker: While he is still speaking, relatives stand outside; notification prompts a gesture and redefinition of family.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining chapter 13 would merge an indoor interruption with a new seaside teaching scene.
units.defensible_basis: Approach-report-question-gesture-saying creates a compact scene.

units.title: Sower parable, purpose, and explanation
units.deciding_marker: A same-day seaside setting initiates the sower story; disciple questioning and a detailed explanation complete its interpretive arc.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting public telling from explanation is possible, but the explanation explicitly returns to the same story.
units.defensible_basis: Story, audience question, and matching element-by-element explanation cohere.

units.title: Weeds, mustard seed, and leaven
units.literary_form: public parable sequence with narrator comment
units.deciding_marker: Another parable introduces a longer field story, followed by two brief growth images; a narrator note closes the public parable session.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at verse 33 would detach the narrator's formal description of this speaking mode.
units.defensible_basis: Repeated he-set-before-them formula and public-session coda unify the sequence.

units.title: Explanation of the weeds
units.deciding_marker: Leaving the crowds and entering the house changes audience; a request elicits an element-by-element explanation and concluding call to hear.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining verses 44-52 would merge requested exposition with a new series of compact analogies.
units.defensible_basis: Private setting, explicit request, and systematic explanation form a discrete unit.

units.title: Treasure, pearl, net, and householder
units.deciding_marker: Repeated the-kingdom-is-like formulas present two value images and a net image, followed by comprehension dialogue and a final householder comparison.
units.rejected_alternative: Separating the final saying would detach the explicit response to the disciples' claimed understanding.
units.defensible_basis: Formulaic series and closing teacher-scribe analogy complete the discourse movement.

units.title: Rejection in his hometown
units.literary_form: hometown encounter narrative with discourse coda
units.deciding_marker: The explicit completion formula ends the parables and departure leads to hometown teaching, astonishment, offense, and limited action.
units.rejected_alternative: Keeping verse 53 with the preceding unit is plausible, but it functions as both closure and launch into a changed setting.
units.defensible_basis: Discourse closure plus new-place response scene yields a defensible combined transition episode.

units.title: Herod hears; John's death recounted
units.deciding_marker: Herod's report about Jesus triggers a backward explanation of arrest, banquet, execution, and burial notification.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at verse 2 would strand the narrative explanation introduced by for.
units.defensible_basis: The retrospective causal frame encloses a complete court tragedy.

units.title: Feeding the five thousand
units.deciding_marker: Hearing the news prompts boat withdrawal; crowds follow, evening need arises, food is multiplied, and a counted satisfaction closes the event.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the following voyage would merge shore provision with a new nocturnal sea setting.
units.defensible_basis: Withdrawal, compassion, problem, provision, and numerical close create a full episode.

units.title: Walking on the sea
units.deciding_marker: Immediate embarkation and solitary dismissal establish separation; storm, approach, recognition, Peter's attempt, rescue, calm, and boat confession resolve it.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting Peter's action from the sea approach would fracture the scene's escalating recognition arc.
units.defensible_basis: Continuous boat setting and progressive response unify the narrative.

units.title: Healings at Gennesaret
units.deciding_marker: Crossing over produces a named landing; local recognition, gathering, touching, and generalized healing replace the prior individual drama.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining chapter 15 would merge a geographic summary with a visiting delegation's dispute.
units.defensible_basis: Landing marker and durative crowd activity define a summary unit.

units.title: Tradition, defilement, and explanation
units.deciding_marker: A Jerusalem delegation asks a question; counterquestion, public pronouncement, disciple exchange, and private explanation develop the same defilement issue.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at verse 9 would detach the crowd saying and explanation that supply the controversy's conclusion.
units.defensible_basis: Topic continuity across changing audiences supports one extended controversy unit.

units.title: Canaanite woman's request
units.deciding_marker: Withdrawal into a new region introduces a persistent petitioner; silence, refusal, kneeling, metaphorical exchange, commendation, and healing complete the scene.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the following healings would blur a singular dialogue with a generalized mountain summary.
units.defensible_basis: Distinct geography, sustained repartee, and immediate resolution delimit it.

units.title: Mountain healings and crowd praise
units.deciding_marker: Departure to the sea and mountain seating introduce crowds bringing many impaired people; generalized cures end in collective wonder and praise.
units.rejected_alternative: Combining with the feeding scene would merge summary montage with a specific problem-and-provision narrative.
units.defensible_basis: Setting, durative action, catalog, and generalized response mark the unit.

units.title: Feeding the four thousand
units.deciding_marker: Jesus summons disciples and states the crowd's need; dialogue, multiplication, satisfaction, count, dismissal, and boat departure provide a full arc.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at verse 38 would omit the departure that closes the gathered-crowd setting.
units.defensible_basis: Problem-to-provision sequence plus explicit dismissal defines the episode.

units.title: A sign demanded
units.deciding_marker: New opponents arrive to test with a heavenly-sign request; Jesus answers with weather discernment and a sign refusal before departing.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the boat discussion would cross an interlocutor and setting reset despite shared vocabulary.
units.defensible_basis: Arrival, request, rebuke, refusal, and departure make a closed encounter.

units.title: Leaven misunderstood and explained
units.deciding_marker: Disciples cross and forget bread; a warning is misunderstood, corrected through recalled feedings, and finally understood figuratively.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting before verse 11 would detach the narrator's explicit understanding resolution.
units.defensible_basis: Mistake, rebuke, recollection, clarification, and comprehension form one pedagogical scene.

units.title: Recognition at Caesarea Philippi
units.deciding_marker: Arrival in a named district prompts public-opinion and direct-recognition questions; response, blessing, declaration, and silence command close the exchange.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the forecast would merge recognition dialogue with an explicit from-that-time narrative turn.
units.defensible_basis: Setting, paired questions, climactic answer, and concluding command delimit it.

units.title: First suffering forecast and demands of following
units.deciding_marker: From that time marks a new teaching phase; forecast provokes Peter's objection, followed by rebuke and a disciple-directed demand sequence.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at verse 23 would detach the generalized audience instruction drawn from the confrontation.
units.defensible_basis: Temporal formula, conflict, and extended application cohere.

units.title: Mountain transformation and descent dialogue
units.deciding_marker: A six-day marker and selected companions initiate ascent; transformed appearance, heavenly voice, fear, touch, descent command, and Elijah question complete the scene.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at verse 8 would exclude the descent instructions and interpretation tied to what was seen.
units.defensible_basis: Ascent-descent frame and continued interpretation form one episode.

units.title: A boy restored
units.deciding_marker: Return to the crowd introduces a kneeling father and failed disciples; rebuke and cure lead to a private why-question and explanation.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at verse 18 would detach the disciples' direct inquiry about the same failed attempt.
units.defensible_basis: Public failure-resolution and private explanation make a coherent teaching scene.

units.title: Second suffering forecast
units.deciding_marker: While they gather in Galilee, Jesus delivers a compressed betrayal-death-rising forecast, ending in intense grief.
units.rejected_alternative: Absorbing it into either adjacent scene would erase its concise formula and emotional close.
units.defensible_basis: New gathering notice and succinct speech-response pattern justify independence.

units.title: Temple tax and the fish
units.literary_form: tax question, private dialogue, and wonder instruction
units.deciding_marker: Arrival at Capernaum introduces collectors' question to Peter; house dialogue leads to an accommodation instruction involving a fish.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining chapter 18 would cross from domestic tax dialogue to a new rank question.
units.defensible_basis: Named setting, question, private reasoning, and task command form a compact unit.

units.title: Rank, the child, stumbling, and the lost sheep
units.deciding_marker: At that time disciples ask about rank; a child is placed among them, followed by linked reception, stumbling, contempt, and lost-sheep sayings.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting at verse 5 would detach warnings that repeatedly refer to these little ones.
units.defensible_basis: Question, enacted sign, repeated little-one vocabulary, and concluding recovery image unify the movement.

units.title: Addressing a sibling's wrongdoing
units.deciding_marker: An if-clause shifts to a staged interpersonal procedure; escalation to additional persons and assembly is followed by binding, agreement, and gathered-presence sayings.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining Peter's question would blur procedural second-person counsel with a new speaker-initiated numerical question.
units.defensible_basis: Stepwise conditional form and collective sayings make a distinct paragraph.

units.title: Repeated forgiveness, servant story, application, and discourse closure
units.literary_form: question-led illustrative narrative with narrator coda
units.deciding_marker: Peter's numerical question elicits a counter-number and extended servant story; a direct application leads into the formal discourse completion and departure.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at 18:35 would detach the narrator's explicit major closure, while splitting the story would weaken question-to-application coherence.
units.defensible_basis: Question, sustained narrative illustration, application, and closure formula create a major seam.

units.title: Question about divorce and response
units.deciding_marker: Opponents approach in a new region with a test question; public argument is followed by a disciple exchange about the same matter.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at verse 9 would detach the immediate private response that completes the topic's scene-level handling.
units.defensible_basis: Approach, test, counterquestion, pronouncement, and disciple follow-up form one unit.

units.title: Children brought to Jesus
units.deciding_marker: Then children are brought, disciples rebuke, Jesus counters, places hands, and departs.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the next encounter would merge two approach scenes with different participants and rhetorical functions.
units.defensible_basis: New participants and a complete bring-rebuke-receive-depart arc delimit it.

units.title: Rich questioner, disciple response, vineyard story, and reversal
units.literary_form: encounter expanding into teaching and illustrative narrative
units.deciding_marker: Behold introduces an individual question; departure prompts disciple dialogue, which expands into a vineyard story and closes by repeating the reversal maxim.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at 19:30 would detach the story framed by the same first-last saying, while starting 20:1 alone would lose its for-link.
units.defensible_basis: The repeated reversal maxim encloses encounter, interpretation, and illustration as one arc.

units.title: Third suffering forecast
units.deciding_marker: Going up toward Jerusalem, Jesus takes the twelve aside and gives a detailed sequence of delivery, condemnation, abuse, death, and rising.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the next request would merge a private forecast with a family petition introduced by then.
units.defensible_basis: Travel marker, audience restriction, and tightly sequenced forecast form a short unit.

units.title: Request for seats and teaching on service
units.deciding_marker: Then a mother approaches with her sons; the request, cup dialogue, group indignation, and contrastive instruction answer one status problem.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting at verse 23 would detach the group correction generated by the petition.
units.defensible_basis: Approach-request-response-reaction-instruction progression unifies the scene.

units.title: Two blind men near Jericho
units.deciding_marker: Departure from Jericho and a following crowd frame two roadside petitioners; rebuke, intensified cry, question, touch, sight, and following close the episode.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining chapter 21 would cross from road departure to a newly staged village approach.
units.defensible_basis: Geographic marker and complete petition-to-following arc define the unit.

units.title: Entry into Jerusalem
units.deciding_marker: Approach to Jerusalem triggers a two-disciple errand; acquisition, mounted entry, crowd acclamation, city stir, and public identification complete the procession.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at verse 9 would omit the city's response to the same entry.
units.defensible_basis: Approach, preparation, procession, acclamation, and arrival response form one event.

units.title: Temple action, healings, and protest
units.deciding_marker: Entry into the temple begins expulsion and overturning; healings and children's cries provoke a protest answered before an overnight departure.
units.rejected_alternative: Combining with the city entry would blur procession and interior confrontation despite immediate sequence.
units.defensible_basis: Temple location, enacted disruption, objection, answer, and exit delimit it.

units.title: Fig tree and faith saying
units.deciding_marker: Morning return and hunger introduce the tree action; its withering prompts marvel and an explanatory saying about faith and prayer.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at verse 19 would detach the explicitly triggered disciple exchange.
units.defensible_basis: Action, immediate result, question, and interpretation create a complete unit.

units.title: Authority challenge and two-sons story
units.deciding_marker: Temple entry brings leaders' authority question; Jesus' counterquestion exposes an impasse and leads to a two-sons comparison applied to them.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at verse 27 would detach the story that directly addresses the challengers after their answer.
units.defensible_basis: Same setting, interlocutors, and application sustain one confrontation movement.

units.title: Tenant farmers story and response
units.literary_form: extended illustrative narrative with controversy reaction
units.deciding_marker: Listen to another parable explicitly begins a new story; its escalation, audience verdict, interpretive sayings, and arrest impulse complete it.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining 22:1 would merge another separately introduced story with a narrator reaction seam.
units.defensible_basis: Explicit introduction, sustained plot, application, and opponents' recognition form a unit.

units.title: Wedding banquet story
units.deciding_marker: Jesus answers again in parables, launching a banquet narrative with invitations, violence, widened gathering, inspection, and closing maxim.
units.rejected_alternative: Absorbing it into the prior tenant story would obscure a new speech introduction and distinct plot world.
units.defensible_basis: Fresh introduction and complete invitation-to-inspection plot establish independence.

units.title: Question about imperial tax
units.deciding_marker: Pharisees withdraw and plan a trap, sending a coalition whose flattering question leads to object demonstration, aphoristic reply, amazement, and departure.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the next question would blur a concluded delegation encounter with a new group's arrival.
units.defensible_basis: Plot, approach, trap, demonstration, answer, and exit form a closed exchange.

units.title: The Sadducees present a hypothetical case
units.deciding_marker: On that day a new group arrives with a denial-based scenario; Jesus rebukes their premise, argues from a quoted saying, and leaves crowds astonished.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting the quotation from the answer would interrupt the argument's culmination.
units.defensible_basis: New interlocutors, extended hypothetical, rebuttal, and crowd response delimit it.

units.title: Question about the greatest commandment
units.deciding_marker: News that the prior group was silenced prompts a gathering and one expert's test; a concise question receives a two-part answer.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining verse 41 would cross from their question to Jesus' counterquestion while retaining the same gathered group.
units.defensible_basis: Approach, single test, balanced response, and closure make a compact unit.

units.title: Jesus questions the Pharisees
units.deciding_marker: While the Pharisees remain gathered, Jesus becomes questioner; a title answer leads to a quotation-based dilemma and a narrator note of silence.
units.rejected_alternative: Combining with the prior test would weaken the role reversal that gives this exchange its force.
units.defensible_basis: Speaker-role reversal and explicit no-one-could-answer closure define the unit.

units.title: Public warning about scribes and Pharisees
units.deciding_marker: Then Jesus addresses crowds and disciples, moving from observed behavior to direct prohibitions on titles and a reversal maxim.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the woes would merge third-person warning with sustained second-person denunciation.
units.defensible_basis: Explicit audience marker, descriptive critique, prohibitions, and maxim form an introductory address.

units.title: Seven woes
units.deciding_marker: The first woe begins a long anaphoric sequence against the same addressees, escalating through paired images to a blood-account climax.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting each woe separately would miss their cumulative catalog form.
units.defensible_basis: Repeated woe formula, vocatives, accusations, and climactic question govern the span.

units.title: Lament over Jerusalem
units.deciding_marker: The addressee shifts from leaders to Jerusalem in direct repeated address; gathering imagery, abandonment, and a future saying close the public speech.
units.rejected_alternative: Absorbing the lament into the woes would flatten the marked vocative and changed emotional form.
units.defensible_basis: Apostrophe, maternal image, and compact three-verse cadence distinguish it.

units.title: Temple departure and private questions
units.deciding_marker: Jesus exits the temple, responds to buildings, then sits on the mountain where disciples privately ask paired questions.
units.rejected_alternative: Starting the discourse at verse 4 alone would detach the narrated setting and exact prompt that organize it.
units.defensible_basis: Movement, visual prompt, relocation, audience restriction, and questions make the discourse frame.

units.title: Opening warnings and beginning troubles
units.deciding_marker: Jesus answers with a deception warning, wars, upheavals, persecution, betrayal, false speakers, endurance, and worldwide proclamation.
units.rejected_alternative: Extending to verse 28 would merge general beginning troubles with a more specific when-you-see instruction.
units.defensible_basis: Direct answer and catalog of preliminary conditions form the opening movement.

units.title: When the desolating sign is seen
units.deciding_marker: A when-you-see clause supplies a specific trigger; rapid imperatives, severity warning, false-sign cautions, and lightning/carcass images follow.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the cosmic sequence would cross the explicit immediately-after transition.
units.defensible_basis: Trigger clause and urgent response instructions unify the section.

units.title: Cosmic signs, coming, and fig-tree lesson
units.deciding_marker: Immediately after marks cosmic change and an appearing sign; gathering follows, then a fig-tree analogy and preservation sayings close the movement.
units.rejected_alternative: Separating the fig-tree lesson would detach the interpretive analogy keyed to all these things.
units.defensible_basis: Temporal reset, climactic imagery, analogy, and assurance form one unit.

units.title: Unknown day and watchfulness
units.deciding_marker: But concerning that day marks an epistemic shift; Noah's days and paired taken-left scenes lead to watch and thief analogies.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the servant illustration would merge direct watch commands with a separately posed who-then story.
units.defensible_basis: Topic reset, repeated ignorance motif, and watchfulness conclusion delimit it.

units.title: Faithful servant, ten attendants, and readiness
units.deciding_marker: Who then begins a servant scenario; its delayed-master contrast flows into then a ten-attendant story, both ending in vigilance under uncertain timing.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting at the chapter boundary is plausible, but then and the shared delay/readiness pattern make one rhetorical arc.
units.defensible_basis: Parallel absent-arrival structures and a common watch conclusion support the cross-chapter unit.

units.title: Entrusted money and returning master
units.deciding_marker: For it is like launches a new departure-and-return story with three servants, parallel reports, contrasted verdicts, and expulsion.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the preceding attendants would merge distinct casts and plots despite a shared delay motif.
units.defensible_basis: Fresh comparison formula, complete plot, and repeated accounting dialogue establish a unit.

units.title: Judgment tableau and discourse closure
units.deciding_marker: When the Son of Man comes opens an enthronement-and-separation scene with two parallel dialogues; the formal completion formula then turns to a time-specific forecast.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at 25:46 would detach the explicit closure that seals the entire discourse, while including 26:2 preserves the transition attached to it.
units.defensible_basis: Balanced right-left dialogues culminate immediately in the major narrator closure.

units.title: Leaders plot arrest
units.deciding_marker: Then leaders assemble in the high priest's court and deliberate deceptive arrest and killing, with a feast-time reservation.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the anointing would merge conspirators' planning location with a separate household act.
units.defensible_basis: New participants, named meeting place, shared plan, and concluding constraint form a short scene.

units.title: Anointing at Bethany
units.deciding_marker: A Bethany house setting introduces a woman pouring costly ointment; disciple indignation prompts a defense and memorial saying.
units.rejected_alternative: Absorbing the following betrayal agreement would blur a public symbolic act with a private transaction.
units.defensible_basis: Stable setting, enacted gesture, objection, interpretation, and close make a complete episode.

units.title: Judas arranges betrayal
units.deciding_marker: Then one of the twelve goes to the priests, asks a price, receives payment, and seeks an opportunity.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining it to the supper would merge advance plotting with a later group gathering.
units.defensible_basis: Departure, negotiation, payment, and ongoing search form a compact counter-scene.

units.title: Passover preparation, betrayal disclosure, and meal
units.literary_form: meal narrative with embedded dialogue and ritual speech
units.deciding_marker: The first day supplies a preparation question and directed errand; evening gathering leads through betrayer dialogue, shared bread and cup, hymn, and departure.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting preparation, disclosure, and meal is possible, but all remain framed by one prepared feast and table setting.
units.defensible_basis: Preparation-to-departure frame and continuous supper context support the span.

units.title: Scattering forecast and Peter's denial claim
units.deciding_marker: Then Jesus predicts collective stumbling and renewed gathering; Peter's protest elicits a specific denial forecast and emphatic counterclaim.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining Gethsemane would merge walking dialogue with a newly named place and selected companions.
units.defensible_basis: Forecast, objection, sharpened prediction, and repeated protest create a self-contained exchange.

units.title: Prayer at Gethsemane
units.deciding_marker: Arrival at a named place and selection of three companions begin the scene; three prayer cycles alternate with sleeping disciples and culminate in the betrayer's approach.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting each cycle would obscure deliberate repetition and escalation.
units.defensible_basis: Place, repeated withdrawal-return pattern, and final rise command unify the passage.

units.title: Betrayal and arrest
units.deciding_marker: While he is still speaking, Judas arrives with an armed crowd; signal, seizure, weapon response, sayings, and disciple flight complete the confrontation.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending before verse 56 would detach the universal flight that resolves the arrest scene.
units.defensible_basis: Arrival, identification, seizure, resistance, explanation, and abandonment form an arc.

units.title: Hearing before the high priest
units.deciding_marker: Those who seized Jesus lead him to the assembled council; testimony fails, a direct question receives an answer, judgment follows, and abuse closes the hearing.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining Peter's denial would merge interior hearing with the courtyard counter-scene despite narrative interweaving.
units.defensible_basis: Location, tribunal participants, testimony sequence, verdict, and abuse delimit the scene.

units.title: Peter's three denials
units.deciding_marker: Peter's courtyard position becomes focal; three escalating recognitions and denials culminate in the rooster, remembered saying, departure, and weeping.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining chapter 27 would cross from individual collapse to morning council action.
units.defensible_basis: Repeated accusation-denial pattern and explicit recollection close the unit.

units.title: Morning delivery and Judas's remorse
units.deciding_marker: Morning council action delivers Jesus to the governor; Judas sees the condemnation, returns the money, dies, and the priests decide its use.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at verse 2 would detach the parallel consequence for the betrayer that the narrator immediately develops.
units.defensible_basis: Temporal transition and money-return sequence form a distinct aftermath before the governor scene resumes.

units.title: Hearing before Pilate and Barabbas choice
units.deciding_marker: Jesus stands before the governor; questioning, feast custom, crowd manipulation, repeated exchange, handwashing, and release-over conclude the decision.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting at verse 14 would isolate preliminary questioning from the same governor-led adjudication.
units.defensible_basis: Stable judicial setting and decision progression define the unit.

units.title: Soldiers mock Jesus
units.deciding_marker: The governor's soldiers take Jesus inside, assemble, clothe, crown, acclaim, spit, strike, strip, and lead him away.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the crucifixion journey would merge the enclosed mock ritual with movement outside toward the execution site.
units.defensible_basis: Location shift and tightly patterned abusive actions form a discrete scene.

units.title: Crucifixion and mockery
units.deciding_marker: Going out introduces Simon and the place of crucifixion; drink, fastening, divided clothing, charge, companions, and three groups of mockers fill the scene.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at verse 38 would detach the sustained taunts that characterize the execution setting.
units.defensible_basis: Procession, execution actions, and repeated ridicule remain within one setting.

units.title: Death and immediate signs
units.literary_form: death scene with portent and confession
units.deciding_marker: From the sixth hour darkness marks a temporal turn; a cry, misunderstanding, final shout, death, torn curtain, earth signs, and guard fear culminate together.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the observing women would shift from immediate signs and confession to a narrator identification aside.
units.defensible_basis: Temporal marker, final actions, portents, and centurion response form the climax.

units.title: Women observe and Jesus is buried
units.deciding_marker: Many women are identified at a distance; evening brings Joseph's request, wrapping, tomb placement, stone, and the women's continued presence.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting verse 55-56 alone is possible, but their observation frames the burial's concluding seated watchers.
units.defensible_basis: Repeated women-at-a-distance/tomb presence encloses the burial action.

units.title: The tomb is secured
units.deciding_marker: The next day priests and Pharisees approach Pilate with a remembered saying and security request; permission leads to sealing and guarding.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining chapter 28 would combine preventive official action with a new dawn visit and disruptive event.
units.defensible_basis: New day, official delegation, request, authorization, and compliance form a unit.

units.title: Women at the tomb and encounter on the way
units.deciding_marker: After the Sabbath, two women arrive; earthquake, messenger action and speech, fearful-joyful departure, and Jesus' greeting and repeated instruction complete their journey.
units.rejected_alternative: Ending at verse 8 would detach the en-route encounter that confirms and repeats the message.
units.defensible_basis: Dawn visit, revelation, departure, encounter, and renewed commission form one arc.

units.title: Guards report and counter-story
units.deciding_marker: While the women go, some guards enter the city and report; council deliberation produces payment, scripted speech, protection assurance, and dissemination.
units.rejected_alternative: Joining the final mountain scene would merge an official urban counter-report with the disciples' separate destination.
units.defensible_basis: Simultaneous transition, report, transaction, instruction, and narrator aftermath make a compact unit.

units.title: Meeting on the mountain
units.deciding_marker: The eleven travel to the appointed mountain, see and respond; Jesus approaches with an authority declaration, commission, teaching charge, and presence promise.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting verse 16-17 from the speech would sever arrival and response from the encounter's culminating address.
units.defensible_basis: Named group, appointed setting, approach, direct commission, and final promise close the book.

appeals.note: No external adjudication was requested during blind primary drafting.
